about: Process plan for the Contour TPG322 triangle insert with a ground chipbreaker, on the shop's 10 x 24 manual surface grinder (grinder-1, with its Suburban 6 x 18 magnetic chuck), then a quick check: the shop's own routing (Harig grinder, quick check), and the drawing's note 1, 'Grind chipbreaker on Harig'. The insert is bought ground to size, periphery, nose radii, 11 deg clearance and both faces, and only the chipbreaker is ground here. Carbide holds too weakly on a magnet (C2's 6% cobalt), so it is clamped in a fixture the magnet holds. A manual grinder's table, cross-feed and down-feed are cranked by hand, so each edge's grind is people's work, not a machine cycle. Written by Claude from the drawing (a modelled lookalike, in inches) and the STEP model; every feature below is checked against the model by moonshot/planning/validate.py. Model frame: Z is thickness (the Z=0 face is the bottom, the Z=3.175 face the top), the triangle lies in XY with its inscribed circle centred on the origin, the first edge the one at X=+4.763 (outward +X), its noses' centres at (3.97, ±6.87) and the third nose's at (-7.94, 0). The chipbreaker is a ring round the three edges: a .010 land at the top, a groove .055 wide and .008 deep inside it (the floor at Z=2.972), then the raised plateau. A surface grinder grinds straight slots: the corners of the ring round the noses, which the STEP has at full depth, are the first open decision below.

stock.size_in: .375 IC triangle x .125, 1/32 nose, 11 deg clearance
stock.from: a TPGN 322 C2 insert, bought ground to size with no chipbreaker [proposed: the drawing gives only the finished insert, and its routing's one operation is the chipbreaker on the grinder]

workholding.note: The insert fixture (no record: missing_records) is a hardened steel block with a 60 deg pocket whose walls lean 11 deg to take the insert's flanks, and a finger clamp on the plateau's middle, clear of the wheel; the magnet holds the block. The pocket sets the edge being ground along the table's travel, and the insert is turned 120 deg in it for the next edge, re-seating on its two other flanks. The fixture is set against the chuck's back edge by eye: the land's .010 is held to .XXX's ±.005, which a fixture square by eye within 0.5 deg over the 14 mm groove meets [proposed]

datum.z: the insert's top: the wheel touched down on it and the down-feed dial zeroed
datum.cross: the cutting edge: the wheel's outer side set .010 in inside it with the cross-feed, by the dial from the wheel's side touched on the edge

operations.what: Grind the first edge's chipbreaker: .055 wide and .008 deep, .010 in from the edge, in two cross positions .020 in apart, the table rocked about 3 mm along the edge's middle

speeds.source: The 6 in wheel at 3,450 rpm runs 5,420 sfpm, inside Machinery's Handbook's 5,000-6,000 sfpm for diamond wheels. [proposed: the grinder's spindle speed, which no record gives (a two-pole motor's 3,450 rpm, as 6 x 18 manual grinders run); the down-feed, .0005 in a pass, 16 passes to .008 and two spark-outs, the light end for resin diamond on carbide; coolant, as carbide's cobalt dust is not to be breathed]. The stroke is what the slot's ends allow: see open

operations.what: Grind the second edge's chipbreaker: the insert turned 120 deg in its pocket and clamped, then ground as the first
Grind the third edge's chipbreaker: the insert turned another 120 deg and clamped, then ground as the first

open.why: The STEP's groove is a ring at full depth round all three noses. A surface grinder's wheel cuts a straight slot along an edge and runs out along its own arc at each end of the stroke (5.6 mm for a 6 in wheel at .008 deep; 7.2 mm for the grinder's 10 in, which can't reach .008 anywhere on a 16.5 mm edge without touching the next edge's land). A slot along one edge must end 1.25 mm short of the sharp corner, or it notches the next edge's cutting edge and the nose. So each edge's groove reaches the STEP's floor within 0.1 mm over 10.7 mm of its 16.5 mm (from 2.9 to 13.6 mm along it), and round each nose it is left up to .008 above the STEP's floor.
